clinician.trajectory_summary: A 79-year-old male on hemodialysis for chronic renal failure presented with persistent cough and recurrent pneumonias over several months. Initial chest radiograph revealed bibasilar infiltrates, right lower lobe atelectasis, bilateral volume loss, and a rounded opaque structure at the level of the right main bronchus. This opaque structure was documented on radiographs obtained 1-2 months prior to the current presentation, indicating a chronic foreign body. Subsequent chest CT confirmed a round dense structure within the right main bronchus, consistent with an aspirated foreign body. A bronchoscopic procedure was performed, and a metal dental crown was successfully removed from the right main bronchus. The aspiration of the metal dental crown was the underlying cause of the patient's recurrent post-obstructive pneumonias and persistent cough.
